title: Why Your Reaction Time Is Faster When You Expect It
hook: You react faster when you expect something to happen.

narration.text: Your reaction time is faster when you know a stimulus is coming.
This is because your brain prepares for the incoming information.
It creates a temporary neural pathway, ready to fire instantly.
This pre-activation allows a quicker response than an unexpected event.
You can test this with a friend and a ruler.
Have them drop it without warning, then with a 'now'.
You will catch it faster when you are ready.
Try it right now and tell me if it worked on you, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Have you ever noticed your reaction times differ? This video explains the science behind why you react faster when you're expecting something to happen. Discover the fascinating neural mechanisms at play and try a simple experiment at home to see it for yourself.
topic: Why your reaction time is faster when you are expecting a stimulus. You can test this with a friend and a ruler.
